bounded_statement: The report's selected result labels a rate as the transit-like dip detection rate of the complete planned target list of 40 stars, but the rate is computed as 6 detections divided by the 32 retained (screened) stars, yielding 0.1875 (18.75%) instead of the complete-domain rate 6/40 = 0.1500 (15.00%). A retained-subset denominator is thus presented as the occurrence rate of the complete planned domain, inflating the headline rate by 3.75 percentage points relative to the stated scientific target.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is arithmetically transparent: the selected-result line and the protocol-status section both disclose that the denominator is the 32 screened stars, so a careful reader could reconstruct the subset scope. This does not falsify the issue because the quantity is explicitly and repeatedly labeled as the detection rate of the complete planned target list of 40 stars, and the per-field breakdown likewise reports only per-screened-star rates, so the report supplies no rate whose denominator matches the declared complete-domain target.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: denominator disclosed but scope label remains the complete planned list; per-field rates also use retained denominators

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the demonstrated-issue verdict three ways. (1) Reframing: perhaps 'detection rate of the complete planned target list' could legitimately mean a rate conditioned on screening; but the task fixes the scientific target as the complete planned set, the report itself defines the target as all 40 stars, and the protocol-status section rules out any amendment redefining the target, so the 6/32 quantity cannot be the requested estimand. (2) Transparency defense: the denominator is disclosed inline; however disclosure of the arithmetic does not change that the headline scope label attributes a retained-subset rate to the complete domain, and no complete-domain rate (6/40) appears anywhere in the report. (3) Data check: I recomputed planned=40, retained=32, events=6 from the CSV to confirm the mismatch is real (0.1875 vs the complete-domain 0.1500) and not a labeling typo with correct arithmetic underneath. All three attempts failed to overturn the verdict.

root_cause: In workflow/analysis.py the selected rate is computed with retained_units (32) as denominator (rate = quantized(events, retained_units, ...)) while the surrounding report text, generated by the same script, declares the scientific target and the reported rate's scope to be the complete planned target list of 40 stars, with no protocol amendment or approved deviation to redefine the target.
